title: Example: simple animation (moving circle)

visuals.title: The notes' moving circle: watch the frames play
A car whose parts move together (x + offset)
A ball falling: the loop variable is y this time

goal: After this you can make a shape move with a for loop: draw, wait, clear, move, repeat, and change the speed, direction and step size.
warmup: A flip-book cartoon in a school notebook: on each page the drawing is a tiny bit different, and when you flick the pages fast your eye sees movement. An animation on the computer is exactly that: draw the picture, wait a moment, erase it, draw it again slightly moved, and repeat.
definition: Animation means showing many pictures (frames) one after another, each with the shape in a slightly new position. In graphics.h the recipe is: draw, delay, cleardevice, move, repeat. A for loop is perfect for it, because the loop variable (for example x) IS the position and it changes by a small step on every pass. graphics.h is not standard C++. It runs only on a lab PC with Turbo C++ (DOSBox) or Code::Blocks/Dev-C++ plus the WinBGIm library, so the in-page compiler cannot run these programs. The canvas on this page is a simulation that draws what the same calls would draw. On the page, the canvas plays the frames of the loop so you can see the movement.
howItWorks: Look at the loop for (int x = 50; x <= 550; x += 5). x starts at 50, grows by 5 each time, and stops after 550, so there are (550 - 50) / 5 + 1 = 101 frames. In each pass: cleardevice() wipes the old picture, setcolor and circle(x, 240, 30) draw the new one at the new x, and delay(30) waits 30 milliseconds, so the whole run takes about 101 x 30 ms = 3 seconds. Speed has two knobs: the step size (a bigger step jumps farther each frame, so it moves faster but less smoothly) and the delay (a smaller delay means more frames per second, so it moves faster). Direction comes from the loop: x going up moves right, y going up moves DOWN the screen (remember y grows downwards). To move several parts together, draw each one at x plus a fixed offset, like the car below. Bouncing, in words: move right until a wall is reached, then count back down so the shape moves left, and repeat. On real BGI the picture can flicker because cleardevice blanks the whole screen before every redraw; programs avoid this with double buffering (draw on a hidden page and show it when ready), which is beyond this course.
syntax:
for (int x = 50; x <= 550; x += 5)   // start, stop, STEP size
{
    cleardevice();                    // 1. erase the old picture
    setcolor(GREEN);                  // 2. color before drawing
    circle(x, 240, 30);               // 3. draw at the NEW position
    delay(30);                        // 4. wait 30 ms (speed)
}                                     // 5. repeat with the next x

mistakes.error: No compiler error, but without cleardevice the old circles stay on the screen and make a long smeared band.
No compiler error. Without delay the loop runs so fast that the circle seems to jump to the end at once.
No compiler error, but nothing moves, because the circle's x never uses the loop variable.

mistakes.right:
for (int y = 40; y <= 420; y += 10)
    circle(320, y, 25);   // y grows downwards
mistakes.error: No compiler error. The ball moves UP the screen, because decreasing y means going toward the top.

mistakes.wrong:
cleardevice();
circle(x, 240, 30);   // road line is not redrawn
mistakes.error: No compiler error. cleardevice erases the WHOLE screen, so anything that must stay visible (road, text) has to be redrawn inside the loop.

examTips: Write the recipe in the answer: draw, delay, cleardevice, move, repeat.
The loop variable must appear in the shape's coordinates, otherwise nothing moves.
delay controls speed. Frames = (stop - start) / step + 1; time = frames x delay.
Everything that should stay visible must be redrawn inside the loop after cleardevice.
Know that y increases downwards, so falling means y += step.
romanSummary: Animation ka formula: draw, delay, cleardevice, position badlo, phir repeat.
for loop ka variable (jaise x) shape ki position hota hai; har dafa step (jaise 5) se barhta hai.
delay(ms) speed control karta hai: chhota delay matlab tez, bara delay matlab slow.
cleardevice na likhein to purani shapes screen par reh jati hain aur lakeer ban jati hai.
Neeche girne ke liye y barhao kyun ke y neeche ki taraf barhta hai. Real BGI mein flicker aa sakta hai, double buffering se door hota hai.

practice.prompt: What does cleardevice() do inside an animation loop?
options: Erases the old picture before the new one is drawn
practice.answer: Erases the old picture before the new one is drawn
practice.hint: Without it the circle leaves a trail.
practice.explanation: cleardevice wipes the whole graphics screen so only the new frame is visible.

practice.prompt: Which function slows the animation down?
practice.explanation: delay(ms) pauses the program, and so controls the speed.

practice.prompt: How many frames does for (int x = 50; x <= 550; x += 5) draw?
practice.explanation: x takes the values 50, 55, ... 550, which is 100 steps plus the first value = 101 frames.

practice.prompt:
Complete the loop so the circle moves from x = 100 to x = 500 in steps of 10.

for (int x = 100; x <= 500; x ___ 10)
practice.explanation: x += 10 adds 10 to x after every pass.

practice.hint: Which number must change each pass?
practice.explanation: The circle's x must use the loop variable x; with 100 it is drawn at the same place every frame.

practice.prompt: To make the animation run twice as fast WITHOUT changing the step, which change works?
options: Halve the delay (delay(15) instead of delay(30))
practice.answer: Halve the delay (delay(15) instead of delay(30))
practice.explanation: Half the waiting time per frame means twice as many frames per second.

practice.prompt: Write a graphics program that moves a yellow circle of radius 20 DOWN the screen at x = 320 from y = 50 to y = 400 in steps of 5, with a delay of 20 ms.
practice.hint: The loop variable is y, because the circle moves down.
practice.explanation: Draw, delay, clear, move, repeat, inside a for loop whose variable is the circle's y. Runs on a lab PC; the page only simulates it.

quiz.prompt: Which is the correct animation recipe?
quiz.explanation: Each frame is drawn, shown for a moment, erased and drawn again in a new place.

quiz.prompt: In the notes' program, what does delay(30) control?
quiz.hint: It is a pause in milliseconds.
quiz.explanation: A shorter pause per frame makes the circle move faster.

quiz.prompt: What makes the circle move to the right?
quiz.hint: The loop variable is the position.
quiz.explanation: circle(x, 240, 30) is drawn farther right each pass because x grows.

quiz.prompt: A ball must fall DOWN the screen. How must its y change?
quiz.explanation: Bigger y means lower on the screen.

quiz.prompt: Why can real BGI animation flicker?
options: The whole screen is cleared and redrawn every frame
quiz.answer: The whole screen is cleared and redrawn every frame
quiz.hint: For a split second the screen is empty.
quiz.explanation: Double buffering (drawing on a hidden page first) is the usual cure.
